#!/usr/bin/env python3
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import re
from pathlib import Path

from tools import k_rule_inventory, klean_export


def sha_bytes(data: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()


def sha_text(text: str) -> str:
    return sha_bytes(text.encode())


def check(label: str, condition: bool, detail: object = "") -> bool:
    print(f"{label}: {'PASS' if condition else 'FAIL'}")
    if detail != "":
        print(f"  {detail}")
    return condition


def main() -> int:
    root = Path("/reference/k-proof")
    generation = Path("/reference/klean-generation")
    generated = generation / "generated"
    discovery = json.loads(Path("/reference/lemma-discovery.json").read_text())
    input_manifest = json.loads((generation / "input-manifest.json").read_text())
    generator_manifest = json.loads((generation / "generator-manifest.json").read_text())
    obligation_map_path = generated / "obligation-map.json"
    obligation_map = json.loads(obligation_map_path.read_text())
    inventory = k_rule_inventory.inventory_verification(root)
    all_ok = True

    print("== Stage 3 classification partition exported into Stage 4 ==")
    discovered_by_id = {r["source_rule_id"]: r for r in discovery["rules"]}
    expected_records = []
    for rule in inventory["rules"]:
        d = discovered_by_id[rule["source_rule_id"]]
        expected_records.append({**rule, "classification": d["classification"], "rationale": d["rationale"]})
    category_keys = {
        "DEFINITION": "definitions",
        "OPERATIONAL_RULE": "operational_rules",
        "PROVED_DERIVED_LEMMA": "proved_derived_lemmas",
        "DOMAIN_LEMMA": "source_rules",
    }
    exported_by_id = {}
    exported_count = 0
    for classification, key in category_keys.items():
        records = input_manifest[key]
        print(f"{key}: {len(records)}")
        for record in records:
            exported_count += 1
            rid = record["source_rule_id"]
            all_ok &= check(f"unique category membership {rid}", rid not in exported_by_id)
            exported_by_id[rid] = record
            all_ok &= check(f"category label {rid}", record["classification"] == classification)
    all_ok &= check("partition count", exported_count == len(expected_records), f"exported={exported_count} inventory={len(expected_records)}")
    all_ok &= check("partition identities", set(exported_by_id) == {r["source_rule_id"] for r in expected_records})
    for expected in expected_records:
        observed = exported_by_id[expected["source_rule_id"]]
        # Stage 4 adds discovery/inventory provenance to DOMAIN_LEMMA records.
        common = {k: observed[k] for k in expected}
        all_ok &= check(f"exact exported record {expected['source_rule_id']}", common == expected)

    print("\n== Stage 4 source/obligation bijection ==")
    domain = [r for r in expected_records if r["classification"] == "DOMAIN_LEMMA"]
    mapped_sources = obligation_map["source_rules"]
    all_ok &= check("domain source order/count", [r["source_rule_id"] for r in mapped_sources] == [r["source_rule_id"] for r in domain])
    obligations = obligation_map["obligations"]
    all_ok &= check("one obligation per domain source", len(obligations) == len(domain) == 1)
    all_ok &= check("obligation IDs unique", len({o["source_rule_id"] for o in obligations}) == len(obligations))
    for source, obligation in zip(domain, obligations):
        all_ok &= check("source-rule identity", obligation["source_rule_id"] == source["source_rule_id"])
        all_ok &= check("source span identity", obligation["source_span"] == {"start_line": source["start_line"], "end_line": source["end_line"]})
        for key in ("normalized_sha256", "inventory_sha256", "discovery_manifest_sha256"):
            all_ok &= check(f"obligation {key}", obligation[key] == mapped_sources[0][key])
        all_ok &= check("Lean conjunct hash", sha_text(obligation["lean_conjunct"]) == obligation["lean_conjunct_sha256"], obligation["lean_conjunct_sha256"])
        print("LEAN_CONJUNCT=<<<")
        print(obligation["lean_conjunct"])
        print(">>>")
        tokens = obligation["lean_conjunct"]
        all_ok &= check("conjunct is not literal True/False", tokens.strip() not in {"True", "False"})
        all_ok &= check("conjunct binds both K rule variables", "(I : SortInt)" in tokens and "(V : SortVal)" in tokens)
        all_ok &= check("conjunct retains guard", "(h : (isInt" in tokens and ") = true)" in tokens)
        all_ok &= check("conjunct retains applyCmp equality", "applyCmp" in tokens and "\u00ab_==Int_\u00bb" in tokens and "\u00abproject:Int\u00bb" in tokens)
        all_ok &= check("conjunct injects right Int into Val", "SortVal.inj_SortInt I" in tokens)

    print("\n== independent recorded-hash checks ==")
    all_ok &= check("obligation-map SHA-256", sha_bytes(obligation_map_path.read_bytes()) == generator_manifest["obligation_map_sha256"], generator_manifest["obligation_map_sha256"])
    all_ok &= check("generated tree SHA-256", klean_export.tree_digest(generated) == generator_manifest["generated_tree_sha256"], generator_manifest["generated_tree_sha256"])
    all_ok &= check("verification source SHA-256", sha_bytes((root / "verification.k").read_bytes()) == input_manifest["verification_sha256"])
    all_ok &= check("Stage 1 export SHA-256", klean_export.tree_digest(root) == input_manifest["stage1_workspace_sha256"])
    all_ok &= check("discovery SHA-256", sha_bytes(Path("/reference/lemma-discovery.json").read_bytes()) == input_manifest["stage3_discovery_manifest_sha256"])
    for parameter in obligation_map["trust_parameters"]:
        binding = {k: parameter[k] for k in ("kore_symbol", "name", "type", "source_rule_ids")}
        digest = sha_text(json.dumps(binding, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")))
        all_ok &= check(f"binding hash {parameter['name']}", digest == parameter["binding_sha256"], digest)

    print("\n== exact fixed target ==")
    lemmas_text = (generated / "Klean105ByLength" / "Lemmas.lean").read_text()
    matches = list(re.finditer(r"(?ms)^\s*def\s+targetStatement\b.*?(?=^\s*end\s+\S+\s*$)", lemmas_text))
    all_ok &= check("exactly one generated target", len(matches) == 1)
    definition = matches[0].group(0).strip()
    expected_definition = klean_export.expected_target_definition(obligation_map)
    all_ok &= check("target is exact mapped conjunction", definition == expected_definition)
    all_ok &= check("target definition hash", sha_text(definition) == generator_manifest["target"]["definition_sha256"], sha_text(definition))
    declaration = "Klean105ByLength.Lemmas.targetStatement"
    statement = " ".join([declaration] + [p["name"] for p in obligation_map["trust_parameters"]])
    all_ok &= check("target statement text", statement == generator_manifest["target"]["statement"], statement)
    all_ok &= check("target statement hash", sha_text(statement) == generator_manifest["target"]["statement_sha256"], sha_text(statement))
    all_ok &= check("manifest target recomputation", klean_export.target_statement(generated) == generator_manifest["target"])
    print("TARGET_DEFINITION=<<<")
    print(definition)
    print(">>>")

    print("\n== source-program relevance ==")
    verification = (root / "verification.k").read_text()
    spec = (root / "spec.k").read_text()
    all_ok &= check("program loop compares value and digit", 'Compare(Name("value"), CmpOp("==", Name("digit")))' in verification)
    all_ok &= check("summary uses projected Int equality", "{X}:>Int ==Int D" in verification)
    all_ok &= check("theorem input guard uses allInts", "requires allInts(VS)" in spec)
    all_ok &= check("domain lemma is used by compiled Stage 1 theory", "applyCmp" in verification and "[simplification]" in verification)

    print(f"\nOVERALL_STAGE4_STRUCTURAL_RESULT={'PASS' if all_ok else 'FAIL'}")
    return 0 if all_ok else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Model-free acceptance check for one Stage 5 Lean proof candidate."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
if str(REPO) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO))

from tools import klean_final_gate


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--generation", required=True, type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--candidate", required=True, type=Path)
    arguments = parser.parse_args(argv)
    gate = subprocess.run(
        ["/usr/local/bin/assert-frozen-toolchain", "agent"],
        text=True,
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
        stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
    )
    if gate.returncode != 0:
        result = {
            "status": "AUDIT_ERROR",
            "error": "frozen toolchain gate failed",
            "toolchain_output_tail": gate.stdout[-4000:],
        }
    else:
        result = klean_final_gate.evaluate_proof_candidate(
            arguments.generation, arguments.candidate
        )
        result["toolchain_gate"] = "PASS"
    print(json.dumps(result, sort_keys=True))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

def _require_bound_inputs(
    audit_input: dict[str, Any],
    observed: dict[str, Any],
) -> None:
    expected = audit_input["resolution"]["hashes"]
    for key, digest in observed.items():
        if expected.get(key) != digest:
            raise KleanFinalGateError(
                f"Stage 6 {key} differs from audit input"
            )


def _result_binding(audit_input: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    try:
        document = _audit_input_binding(Path(audit_input))
    except KleanFinalGateError:
        return {}
    return {
        "mode": document["resolution"]["mode"],
        "resolved_input_sha256": document[
            "resolved_input_sha256"
        ],
        "input_hashes": document["resolution"]["hashes"],
    }


def check_final(
    frozen_input: Path,
    discovery_manifest: Path,
    generation: Path,
    candidate: Path | None,
    *,
    toolchain_lock: Path,
    audit_input: Path,
    run_command: Callable[..., tuple[int, str]] = _run,

        signed_resolution["mode"] == "CLASSIFICATION_AND_PROOF"

    ):
        raise KleanFinalGateError(
            "proof-bearing audit requires a Stage 5 Lean candidate"
        )
    if (
        signed_resolution["mode"] == "CLASSIFICATION_ONLY"

    ):

            "classification-only audit must not use a Stage 5 Lean "

        )
    expected_mode = signed_resolution["mode"]
    observed_mode = (
        "CLASSIFICATION_AND_PROOF"
        if candidate is not None
        else "CLASSIFICATION_ONLY"
    )
    if observed_mode != expected_mode:
        raise KleanFinalGateError(
            "Stage 6 mechanical mode differs from audit input"
        )
    before_hashes = _input_hashes(

    _require_bound_inputs(audit_binding, before_hashes)
    try:

    except klean_preflight.KleanPreflightError as error:

    preflight_status = preflight.get("status")

    )

        if target is not None or preflight.get("obligation_count") != 0:

        _require_bound_inputs(audit_binding, after_hashes)
        return {

            "mode": "CLASSIFICATION_ONLY",

            ],
            "input_hashes": signed_resolution["hashes"],

    _require_bound_inputs(audit_binding, after_hashes)

        "generation_sha256": proof_check["generation_sha256"],
        "candidate_sha256": proof_check["candidate_sha256"],
        "used_axioms": proof_check["used_axioms"],
        "diagnostics": proof_check["diagnostics"],
    }


def run_gate(
    frozen_input: Path,
    discovery_manifest: Path,
    generation: Path,
    candidate: Path | None,
    *,
    toolchain_lock: Path,
    audit_input: Path,
    output: Path,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    output = Path(output)
    if output.exists() or output.is_symlink():
        raise KleanFinalGateError(f"output already exists: {output}")
    try:
        document = check_final(
            frozen_input,
            discovery_manifest,
            generation,
            candidate,
            toolchain_lock=toolchain_lock,
            audit_input=audit_input,
        )
    except KleanFinalGateError as error:
        document = {
            "status": "FAIL",
            "error": str(error),
            **_result_binding(audit_input),
        }
    except BaseException as error:
        document = {
            "status": "AUDIT_ERROR",
            "error": f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}",
            **_result_binding(audit_input),
        }
    temporary = output.with_name(f".{output.name}.tmp")
    temporary.write_text(json.dumps(document, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
    os.replace(temporary, output)
    return document


def evaluate_gate(
    frozen_input: Path,
    discovery_manifest: Path,
    generation: Path,
    candidate: Path | None,
    *,
    toolchain_lock: Path,
    audit_input: Path,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    try:
        return check_final(
            frozen_input,
            discovery_manifest,
            generation,
            candidate,
            toolchain_lock=toolchain_lock,
            audit_input=audit_input,
        )
    except KleanFinalGateError as error:
        return {
            "status": "FAIL",
            "error": str(error),
            **_result_binding(audit_input),
        }
    except BaseException as error:
        return {
            "status": "AUDIT_ERROR",
            "error": f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}",
            **_result_binding(audit_input),
        }


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--frozen-k", required=True, type=Path)
    parser.add_argument(
        "--discovery-manifest", required=True, type=Path
    )
    parser.add_argument("--generation", required=True, type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--candidate", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--toolchain-lock", required=True, type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--audit-input", required=True, type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path)
    arguments = parser.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        if arguments.output is None:
            result = evaluate_gate(
                arguments.frozen_k,
                arguments.discovery_manifest,
                arguments.generation,
                arguments.candidate,
                toolchain_lock=arguments.toolchain_lock,
                audit_input=arguments.audit_input,
            )
        else:
            result = run_gate(
                arguments.frozen_k,
                arguments.discovery_manifest,
                arguments.generation,
                arguments.candidate,
                toolchain_lock=arguments.toolchain_lock,
                audit_input=arguments.audit_input,
                output=arguments.output,
            )
    except KleanFinalGateError as error:
        print(f"Klean final gate failed: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    print(json.dumps(result, sort_keys=True))
    return 0 if result["status"] == "PASS" else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

At the start of your turn, you are the active agent.
You can spawn sub-agents to handle subtasks, and those sub-agents can spawn their own sub-agents.
All agents in the team, including the agents that you can assign tasks to, are equally intelligent and capable, and have access to the same set of tools.

You can use `spawn_agent` to create a new agent, `followup_task` to give an existing agent a new task and trigger a turn, and `send_message` to pass a message to a running agent without triggering a turn.

// reference/src/semantics/int.k — MPY-INT
// Int cases of the operator dispatch; Python // and % are floored (pyMod).

module MPY-INT
  imports MPY-CORE

  rule applyUn("-", I:Int) => 0 -Int I

  rule applyBin("+",  I1:Int, I2:Int) => I1 +Int I2
  // Bool participates in int arithmetic (x += (a == b))
  rule applyBin("+",  I:Int, B:Bool) => I +Int #if B #then 1 #else 0 #fi
  rule applyBin("+",  B:Bool, I:Int) => #if B #then 1 #else 0 #fi +Int I
  rule applyBin("-",  I1:Int, I2:Int) => I1 -Int I2
  rule applyBin("*",  I1:Int, I2:Int) => I1 *Int I2
  rule applyBin("%",  I1:Int, I2:Int) => pyMod(I1, I2)
  rule applyBin("//", I1:Int, I2:Int) => (I1 -Int pyMod(I1, I2)) /Int I2
  rule applyBin("**", I1:Int, I2:Int) => I1 ^Int I2 requires I2 >=Int 0

  syntax Int ::= pyMod(Int, Int) [function]
  rule pyMod(I1:Int, I2:Int) => ((I1 %Int I2) +Int I2) %Int I2

  rule applyCmp("<",  I1:Int, I2:Int)   => I1 <Int  I2
  rule applyCmp("<=", I1:Int, I2:Int)   => I1 <=Int I2
  rule applyCmp(">",  I1:Int, I2:Int)   => I1 >Int  I2
  rule applyCmp(">=", I1:Int, I2:Int)   => I1 >=Int I2
  rule applyCmp("==", I1:Int, I2:Int)   => I1 ==Int I2
  rule applyCmp("!=", I1:Int, I2:Int)   => I1 =/=Int I2
endmodule
// reference/src/semantics/dict.k — MPY-DICT
//
// Minimal dict support. A dict value is `dictV(KS, VS)`: PARALLEL insertion-ordered key/value
// ValSeqs (Python dict order; keys distinct; re-inserting a key updates its value in place, keeping
// the original position). Concrete for krun (the ordered build + `.keys()` are the real ops); a proof
// over a SYMBOLIC dict passes `dictV(KS, WS)` with a symbolic key sequence KS and reads
// `d.keys() = list(KS)`, then keeps each key opaque problem-locally.
//
// Only the pieces needed so far: a dict VALUE (so `{}` inside a mixed list evaluates and
// `isinstance(x, int)` rejects it), the `{k: v, ...}` literal, and `.keys()`. More dict ops (subscript
// / `.get()` / `.values()` / dict `==`) are added as dict problems need them — kept minimal + additive.

module MPY-DICT
  imports MPY-CORE
  imports MPY-ITER
  imports MPY-METHODS
  imports MPY-LIST

  // dict as PARALLEL ordered key/value ValSeqs (same length; keys distinct).
  syntax Val ::= dictV(ValSeq, ValSeq)

  // ==== DictExpr: {k: v, ...} literal. Eval each key then value, left to right, insert-with-dedup.
  syntax KItem ::= #dictAcc(Entries, ValSeq, ValSeq)
                 | #dictKey(Expr, Entries, ValSeq, ValSeq)
                 | #dictVal(Val, Entries, ValSeq, ValSeq)
  rule <k> DictExpr(ES:Entries) => #dictAcc(ES, .ValSeq, .ValSeq) ... </k>
  rule <k> #dictAcc(.Entries, KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq) => dictV(KS, VS) ... </k>
  rule <k> #dictAcc((Entry(K:Expr, V:Expr), REST:Entries), KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq)
        => K ~> #dictKey(V, REST, KS, VS) ... </k>
  rule <k> KV:Val ~> #dictKey(V:Expr, REST:Entries, KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq)
        => V ~> #dictVal(KV, REST, KS, VS) ... </k>
  rule <k> VV:Val ~> #dictVal(KV:Val, REST:Entries, KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq)
        => #dictAcc(REST, dPutK(KS, KV), dPutV(KS, VS, KV, VV)) ... </k>

  // insert-with-dedup helpers (concrete Val key equality via ==K). [total] so buildFold over a dict is
  // total (its #Ceil is #Top) — needed when a symbolic proof carries a built dict as a config value.
  syntax Bool ::= dHasKey(ValSeq, Val) [function, total]
  rule dHasKey(.ValSeq, _:Val)                => false
  rule dHasKey(vCons(A:Val, _:ValSeq), K:Val) => true          requires A ==K K
  rule dHasKey(vCons(A:Val, R:ValSeq), K:Val) => dHasKey(R, K) requires notBool (A ==K K)

  // dPutK: KS unchanged if K already present, else append K (keep-first-position).
  syntax ValSeq ::= dPutK(ValSeq, Val) [function, total]
  rule dPutK(KS:ValSeq, K:Val) => KS                                  requires dHasKey(KS, K)
  rule dPutK(KS:ValSeq, K:Val) => valSeqConcat(KS, vCons(K, .ValSeq)) requires notBool dHasKey(KS, K)

  // dPutV: parallel to KS — set the value at K's position if present, else append V at the end. The
  // [owise] catch-all covers the degenerate mismatched-length case (never reached for a well-formed dict).
  syntax ValSeq ::= dPutV(ValSeq, ValSeq, Val, Val) [function, total]
  rule dPutV(vCons(A:Val, _:ValSeq), vCons(_:Val, VR:ValSeq), K:Val, V:Val)  => vCons(V, VR)
       requires A ==K K
  rule dPutV(vCons(A:Val, KR:ValSeq), vCons(B:Val, VR:ValSeq), K:Val, V:Val) => vCons(B, dPutV(KR, VR, K, V))
       requires notBool (A ==K K)
  rule dPutV(_KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq, _K:Val, V:Val) => valSeqConcat(VS, vCons(V, .ValSeq)) [owise]

  // ==== dict methods ========================================================
  // d.keys() -> a FRESH list object of the ordered keys (k-cell: it allocates).
  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(dictV(KS:ValSeq, _:ValSeq), "keys")), .Vals)
        => #alloc(list(KS)) ... </k>
       [priority(40)]

  // ==== dict subscript READ: d[k] (assoc lookup; KeyError is out of subset) ==
  rule applyIndexD(dictV(KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq), K:Val) => dGet(KS, VS, K)
  syntax Val ::= applyIndexD(Val, Val) [function]
  rule <k> Subscript(dictV(KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq), K:Val) => applyIndexD(dictV(KS, VS), K) ... </k>
       [priority(45)]

  // ==== dict subscript-assign: d[k] = v (insert/update in place) =============
  // Only for a LOCAL dict variable X (the current scope holds it). Reuses dPutK/dPutV.
  syntax Val ::= dictSet(Val, Val, Val) [function]
  rule dictSet(dictV(KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq), K:Val, V:Val) => dictV(dPutK(KS, K), dPutV(KS, VS, K, V))

  // RHS evaluates first (Assign strictness), then the key. Dispatch on the scope
  // value: a bare dict updates in the scope (dicts stay values); a ref (a heap
  // list — or a heap dict later) writes the heap in place.
  syntax KItem ::= #dsetK(String, Val)
  rule <k> Assign(Subscript(Name(X:String), K:Expr), VV:Val) => K ~> #dsetK(X, VV) ... </k>
  rule <k> KV:Val ~> #dsetK(X:String, VV:Val) => .K ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ X <- dictSet({M[X]}:>Val, KV, VV) ], _) ... </scopes>
       requires X in_keys(M) andBool notBool isRefV({M[X]}:>Val)
  rule <k> KV:Val ~> #dsetK(X:String, VV:Val) => #dsetV({M[X]}:>Val, KV, VV) ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
       requires X in_keys(M) andBool isRefV({M[X]}:>Val)
  syntax KItem ::= #dsetV(Val, Val, Val)
  rule <k> #dsetV(ref(H:Int), I:Int, VV:Val) => .K ... </k>
       <heap> ... H |-> list(VS:ValSeq => setVSAt(VS, normIdxD(I, vsLen(VS)), VV)) ... </heap>
  // negative-index normalization local to the write (subscript.k's is not imported here)
  syntax Int ::= normIdxD(Int, Int) [function, total]
  rule normIdxD(I:Int, LEN:Int) => I +Int LEN requires I  <Int 0
  rule normIdxD(I:Int, _:Int)   => I          requires I >=Int 0

  // ==== dict == (order-insensitive: same size + same key->value pairs) =======
  rule applyCmp("==", dictV(KS1:ValSeq, VS1:ValSeq), dictV(KS2:ValSeq, VS2:ValSeq))
    => (vsLen(KS1) ==Int vsLen(KS2)) andBool dSubset(KS1, VS1, KS2, VS2)
  syntax Bool ::= dSubset(ValSeq, ValSeq, ValSeq, ValSeq) [function]
  rule dSubset(.ValSeq, .ValSeq, _:ValSeq, _:ValSeq) => true
  rule dSubset(vCons(K:Val, KR:ValSeq), vCons(V:Val, VR:ValSeq), KS2:ValSeq, VS2:ValSeq)
    => dHasKey(KS2, K) andBool (dGet(KS2, VS2, K) ==K V) andBool dSubset(KR, VR, KS2, VS2)
  syntax Val ::= dGet(ValSeq, ValSeq, Val) [function]
  rule dGet(vCons(A:Val, _:ValSeq), vCons(B:Val, _:ValSeq), K:Val) => B                requires A ==K K
  rule dGet(vCons(A:Val, KR:ValSeq), vCons(_:Val, VR:ValSeq), K:Val) => dGet(KR, VR, K) requires notBool (A ==K K)
endmodule
// reference/src/semantics/set.k — MPY-SET

module MPY-SET
  imports MPY-CORE

  // a set value, carried as its distinct codes in first-seen order (order is irrelevant
  // to membership/cardinality — the two observations sets support here).
  syntax Val ::= setV(IntSeq)

  // membership of a code in the accumulated distinct-code sequence
  syntax Bool ::= codeIn(Int, IntSeq) [function, total]
  rule codeIn(_:Int, .IntSeq)                => false
  rule codeIn(C:Int, iCons(H:Int, T:IntSeq)) => C ==Int H orBool codeIn(C, T)

  // the distinct codes of CS (insert-if-absent fold, first-seen order)
  syntax IntSeq ::= dedupCodes(IntSeq)         [function, total]
                  | dedupFrom(IntSeq, IntSeq)  [function, total]
  rule dedupCodes(CS:IntSeq) => dedupFrom(CS, .IntSeq)
  rule dedupFrom(.IntSeq, ACC:IntSeq) => ACC
  rule dedupFrom(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq), ACC:IntSeq) => dedupFrom(S, ACC)
       requires codeIn(C, ACC)
  rule dedupFrom(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq), ACC:IntSeq) => dedupFrom(S, snocCode(ACC, C))
       requires notBool codeIn(C, ACC)

  syntax IntSeq ::= snocCode(IntSeq, Int) [function, total]
  rule snocCode(.IntSeq, C:Int)                => iCons(C, .IntSeq)
  rule snocCode(iCons(H:Int, T:IntSeq), C:Int) => iCons(H, snocCode(T, C))

  // ==== set equality: two sets are equal iff mutually subsuming ==============
  // subsetCodes(A, B) — every code of A occurs in B (duplicates in A are harmless).
  syntax Bool ::= subsetCodes(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
  rule subsetCodes(.IntSeq, _:IntSeq)                => true
  rule subsetCodes(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq), B:IntSeq) => codeIn(C, B) andBool subsetCodes(S, B)

  syntax Bool ::= sameSet(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
  rule sameSet(A:IntSeq, B:IntSeq) => subsetCodes(A, B) andBool subsetCodes(B, A)

  // set == set  (the only comparison sets support here)
  rule applyCmp("==", setV(A:IntSeq), setV(B:IntSeq)) => sameSet(A, B)
endmodule

import Proof

namespace BridgeAudit

open Proof

def intK (i : SortInt) : SortK :=
  SortK.kseq (SortKItem.inj_SortInt i) SortK.dotk

-- Concrete positive and adversarial cases for each target parameter.
example : Proof.«_==Int_» 17 17 = true := by rfl
example : Proof.«_==Int_» (-4) 17 = false := by rfl
example : Proof.isInt (intK (-4)) = true := by rfl
example : Proof.«project:Int» (intK (-4)) = -4 := by rfl
example :
    Proof.«applyCmp(_,_,_)_MPY-CORE_Bool_String_Val_Val»
      "==" (SortVal.inj_SortInt 17) (SortVal.inj_SortInt 17) = true := by
  rfl
example :
    Proof.«applyCmp(_,_,_)_MPY-CORE_Bool_String_Val_Val»
      "==" (SortVal.inj_SortInt (-4)) (SortVal.inj_SortInt 17) = false := by
  rfl
example :
    Proof.isInt
      (SortK.kseq
        (SortKItem.inj_SortBool true)
        SortK.dotk) = false := by
  rfl

-- A counterfactual: coordinated constant definitions make the generated
-- equation provable, despite not implementing K.  This is an adversarial
-- witness that target proof alone is insufficient and bridge auditing matters.
def badEq (_left _right : SortInt) : SortBool := false
def badApply (_operator : SortString) (_left _right : SortVal) : SortBool := false

theorem coordinatedConstantsCanProveTarget :
    Klean105ByLength.Lemmas.targetStatement
      badEq badApply Proof.isInt Proof.«project:Int» := by
  intro I V h
  rfl

-- Mutating only applyCmp does not satisfy the frozen equation on equal ints.
example :
    badApply "==" (SortVal.inj_SortInt 17) (SortVal.inj_SortInt 17) ≠
      Proof.«_==Int_» (Proof.«project:Int» (intK 17)) 17 := by
  decide

-- Mutating equality alone also fails on the same frozen operational case.
example :
    Proof.«applyCmp(_,_,_)_MPY-CORE_Bool_String_Val_Val»
        "==" (SortVal.inj_SortInt 17) (SortVal.inj_SortInt 17) ≠
      badEq (Proof.«project:Int» (intK 17)) 17 := by
  decide

end BridgeAudit

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Model-free Stage 6 gate for Klean classification and optional proof."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Callable

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
if str(REPO) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO))

from tools import (
    klean_export,
    klean_preflight,
    pipeline_contract,
    stage6_resolution_contract,
)


class KleanFinalGateError(RuntimeError):
    pass


def _run(
    command: list[str],
    *,
    cwd: Path,
    timeout: int,
) -> tuple[int, str]:
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(
            command,
            cwd=cwd,
            timeout=timeout,
            text=True,
            stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
            stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
        )
        return result.returncode, result.stdout
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        return 124, f"TIMEOUT after {timeout}s"


def _regular_json(path: Path, label: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    if not path.is_file() or path.is_symlink():
        raise KleanFinalGateError(f"{label} is not a regular file")
    try:
        document = json.loads(path.read_text())
    except (OSError, ValueError) as error:
        raise KleanFinalGateError(f"{label} is malformed") from error
    if not isinstance(document, dict):
        raise KleanFinalGateError(f"{label} must be a JSON object")
    return document


def _candidate_gate(candidate: Path, target: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    entries = klean_export._tree_entries(candidate)
    proof = candidate / "Proof.lean"
    if not proof.is_file() or proof.is_symlink():
        raise KleanFinalGateError("candidate is missing regular Proof.lean")
    for required in ("lakefile.lean", "lean-toolchain"):
        path = candidate / required
        if not path.is_file() or path.is_symlink():
            raise KleanFinalGateError(f"candidate is missing regular {required}")
    candidate_sources: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    for relative, kind, path in entries:
        if kind != "file" or path.suffix != ".lean":
            continue
        text = path.read_text()
        if Path(relative).parts[0] != "Base":
            candidate_sources.append((relative, text))
        forbidden = re.search(
            r"\b(?:sorry|admit|unsafe|axiom|opaque)\b", text
        )
        if forbidden is not None:
            raise KleanFinalGateError(
                f"candidate contains forbidden Lean token "
                f"{forbidden.group(0)!r} in {relative}"
            )
    statement = target.get("statement")
    parameters = target.get("parameters")
    if not isinstance(statement, str) or not statement:
        raise KleanFinalGateError("generator target statement is malformed")
    if not isinstance(parameters, list):
        raise KleanFinalGateError("generator target bindings are malformed")
    proof_text = proof.read_text()
    for parameter in parameters:
        if not isinstance(parameter, dict):
            raise KleanFinalGateError("generator target binding is malformed")
        name = parameter.get("name")
        lean_type = parameter.get("type")
        if not isinstance(name, str) or not isinstance(lean_type, str):
            raise KleanFinalGateError("generator target binding is malformed")
        declarations = [
            (relative, match.start())
            for relative, text in candidate_sources
            for match in re.finditer(
                rf"(?m)^\s*(?:@\[[^\n]*\]\s*)*"
                rf"(?:noncomputable\s+)?def\s+{re.escape(name)}"
                rf"\s*(?::|\()",
                text,
            )
        ]
        if len(declarations) != 1:
            raise KleanFinalGateError(
                f"candidate must define exact trust binding {name!r} once"
            )
    theorem_matches = re.findall(
        r"(?ms)^\s*theorem\s+final\s*:\s*(.*?)\s*:=\s*by\b",
        proof_text,
    )
    if len(theorem_matches) != 1:
        raise KleanFinalGateError(
            "candidate must contain exactly one theorem final"
        )
    if " ".join(theorem_matches[0].split()) != " ".join(statement.split()):
        raise KleanFinalGateError(
            "Proof.final does not state the exact generated target"
        )


def _allowed_axioms(inventory: dict[str, Any]) -> set[str]:
    allowlist = inventory.get("allowlist")
    if not isinstance(allowlist, list):
        raise KleanFinalGateError("trust inventory allowlist is malformed")
    names = {"Classical.choice", "propext", "Quot.sound"}
    for entry in allowlist:
        if not isinstance(entry, dict):
            raise KleanFinalGateError("trust inventory entry is malformed")
        name = entry.get("name")
        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
            raise KleanFinalGateError("trust inventory name is malformed")
        names.add(name)
    return names


def _parse_axioms(output: str) -> set[str]:
    matches = list(re.finditer(r"depends on axioms:\s*\[", output))
    axiom_free = re.findall(
        r"does not depend on any axioms", output
    )
    if len(matches) + len(axiom_free) != 1:
        raise KleanFinalGateError("#print axioms output is missing or ambiguous")
    if axiom_free:
        return set()
    tokens: list[str] = []
    token: list[str] = []
    quoted = False
    for character in output[matches[0].end() :]:
        if character == "«" and not quoted:
            quoted = True
            token.append(character)
        elif character == "»" and quoted:
            quoted = False
            token.append(character)
        elif character == "," and not quoted:
            name = "".join(token).strip()
            if not name:
                raise KleanFinalGateError(
                    "#print axioms output contains an empty axiom name"
                )
            tokens.append(name)
            token = []
        elif character == "]" and not quoted:
            name = "".join(token).strip()
            if name:
                tokens.append(name)
            return set(tokens)
        else:
            token.append(character)
    raise KleanFinalGateError("#print axioms output has no closing bracket")


def check_proof_candidate(
    generation: Path,
    candidate: Path,
    *,
    run_command: Callable[..., tuple[int, str]] = _run,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Independently build and axiom-check one immutable Stage 5 proof."""

    generation = Path(generation)
    candidate = Path(candidate)
    manifest = _regular_json(
        generation / "generator-manifest.json", "generator manifest"
    )
    target = manifest.get("target")
    if not isinstance(target, dict):
        raise KleanFinalGateError("generator target is malformed")
    before_generation = klean_export.tree_digest(generation)
    before_candidate = klean_export.tree_digest(candidate)
    _candidate_gate(candidate, target)
    inventory = _regular_json(
        generation / "trust-inventory.json", "trust inventory"
    )
    diagnostics: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="klean-proof-check-") as temporary:
        project = Path(temporary) / "project"
        shutil.copytree(candidate, project)
        if klean_export.tree_digest(project) != before_candidate:
            raise KleanFinalGateError(
                "candidate changed while copying for mechanical audit"
            )
        shutil.rmtree(project / ".lake", ignore_errors=True)
        shutil.rmtree(project / "Base", ignore_errors=True)
        shutil.copytree(generation / "generated", project / "Base")
        audit_source = project / "AxiomAudit.lean"
        audit_source.write_text(
            "import Proof\n\n"
            "namespace Proof\n\n"
            f"#check (final : {target['statement']})\n"
            "#print axioms final\n\n"
            "end Proof\n"
        )
        outputs: dict[tuple[str, ...], str] = {}
        commands = (
            ["lake", "clean"],
            ["lake", "build"],
            ["lake", "env", "lean", "AxiomAudit.lean"],
        )
        for command in commands:
            code, output = run_command(command, cwd=project, timeout=600)
            diagnostics.append(
                {
                    "command": command,
                    "exit_code": code,
                    "output_sha256": hashlib.sha256(
                        output.encode()
                    ).hexdigest(),
                    "output_tail": output[-4000:],
                }
            )
            outputs[tuple(command)] = output
            if code != 0:
                raise KleanFinalGateError(
                    f"{' '.join(command)} failed ({code}): {output[-600:]}"
                )
        used_axioms = _parse_axioms(
            outputs[("lake", "env", "lean", "AxiomAudit.lean")]
        )
    if klean_export.tree_digest(generation) != before_generation:
        raise KleanFinalGateError(
            "generation changed during mechanical audit"
        )
    if klean_export.tree_digest(candidate) != before_candidate:
        raise KleanFinalGateError(
            "candidate changed during mechanical audit"
        )
    if "sorryAx" in used_axioms:
        raise KleanFinalGateError("Proof.final depends on forbidden sorryAx")
    allowed = _allowed_axioms(inventory)
    unexpected = sorted(
        axiom for axiom in used_axioms if axiom not in allowed
    )
    if unexpected:
        raise KleanFinalGateError(
            "Proof.final has unrecorded axiom dependencies: "
            + ", ".join(unexpected)
        )
    return {
        "status": "PASS",
        "target": target,
        "generation_sha256": before_generation,
        "candidate_sha256": before_candidate,
        "used_axioms": sorted(used_axioms),
        "diagnostics": diagnostics,
    }


def evaluate_proof_candidate(
    generation: Path,
    candidate: Path,
    *,
    run_command: Callable[..., tuple[int, str]] = _run,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    try:
        return check_proof_candidate(
            generation, candidate, run_command=run_command
        )
    except KleanFinalGateError as error:
        return {"status": "FAIL", "error": str(error)}
    except BaseException as error:
        return {
            "status": "AUDIT_ERROR",
            "error": f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}",
        }


def _audit_input_binding(path: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    document = _regular_json(path, "Stage 6 audit input")
    try:
        resolution, digest = (
            stage6_resolution_contract.verify_audit_input(document)
        )
    except (
        stage6_resolution_contract.Stage6ResolutionContractError
    ) as error:
        raise KleanFinalGateError(str(error)) from error
    mode = resolution.get("mode")
    hashes = resolution.get("hashes")
    if (
        mode not in {
            "CLASSIFICATION_ONLY",
            "CLASSIFICATION_AND_PROOF",
        }
        or not isinstance(hashes, dict)
    ):
        raise KleanFinalGateError(
            "Stage 6 audit input binding is malformed"
        )
    return {
        "resolution": resolution,
        "resolved_input_sha256": digest,
    }

name: validating-proof
description: 'Use when kprove reports success (#Top) and you must audit proof-local functions, lemmas, or rewrites, theorem intent, or the trust boundary before writing PROOF.md.'
---

## Verification is not validation

`kprove` exiting 0 with `#Top` proves closure under the supplied semantics, claims,
and proof extensions. Before reporting a proof of the program, read the
[proof-extension soundness contract](../shared/proof-extension-soundness.md) and
audit the extensions, intended property, and evidence independently.

## Rebuild the proof-extension inventory

Do not copy the construction record uncritically. Inspect `verification.k`, the
spec module, and imported proof-local modules for functions, totality attributes,
simplification and concrete rules, priority rules, ordinary rewrites, auxiliary
claims, opaque terms, and framed or omitted cells. Reconstruct the contract's
record for every extension contributing to claim closure.

For each operational bridge, identify the fixed-semantics behavior it preempts
and compare binding, evaluation, control, and every affected cell. For each
equational symbol, check guard coverage and pairwise overlap. For each opaque
term, trace whether it affects control, observable state, or the final result.

## Operational-bridge context procedure

For every operational bridge:

1. Reconstruct its complete matched context: LHS, RHS, guards, priority, active
   continuation, control stack, bindings, and framed or omitted cells.
2. Require a bridge-free universal connection theorem over the bridge's
   complete match domain. It must not import the proposed bridge; inspect its
   imports and dependencies to verify that it uses only fixed semantics and
   independently justified theory. Reconstruct the exact justification scope
   from that theorem and check that every bridge match lies inside it; an exact
   trailing computation does not justify an arbitrary continuation frame.
3. Choose a satisfiable boundary witness. Compare the fixed-semantics
   configuration with the corresponding bridge-enabled configuration over the
   result, control state, and every observable cell.
4. When the bridge admits a broader suffix, place an observable continuation
   immediately after the bridged region, such as a distinct result, state
   update, output, allocation, or exception. Fixed and bridge-enabled behavior
   must agree; rejection because the narrowed bridge does not match is also
   valid containment evidence.
5. Record the artifacts, commands, and results. This operational-sensitivity
   check is separate from the false-postcondition mutation in A5: the former
   tests execution fidelity, while the latter tests result constraint.

If a bridge introduces return, frame popping, exception propagation, loop
control, cleanup, or another abrupt effect, a value-only comparison is
insufficient. Any reachable context in which the bridge discards, preserves, or
unwinds different computation is a Gate A failure.

## Result-bearing abstraction procedure

For every fresh, opaque, or newly summarized value:

1. Trace each fresh or opaque symbol through rules and claims. Mark every
   branch, returned value, observable state, exception, and postcondition it can
   influence.
2. Classify its origin. For an **Externally trusted boundary**, confirm that the
   operation is fixed, intentionally outside the program-defined code being
   verified and outside the theorem, and that the proof is
   interpretation-parametric or makes every value-level conclusion conditional
   on the named contract. This path does not require a connection theorem or
   opposite-interpretation witnesses; record the contract and every dependent
   claim. A program-derived abstraction continues through the remaining steps.
3. Check whether the same symbol appears in both an operational bridge and the
   final summary or postcondition. Treat that as a circular dependency, not as
   evidence that the source computation has the same meaning.
4. Require a bridge-free universal connection theorem over the complete matched
   domain showing that fixed semantics produces exactly the abstraction's
   value. The theorem must not import the proposed bridge; verify its imports
   and dependencies use only fixed semantics plus independently justified
   theory. Truthful exhaustive equations may supply the value; a name,
   `[total]`, opacity, or finite differential evidence does not.
5. Choose satisfiable ground witnesses for distinct observable outcomes.
   Compare each fixed-semantics value with bridge-enabled execution, then
   attempt the opposite ground interpretation. If the extended theory admits
   the wrong branch, result, state, or exception—or merely leaves that equality
   unconstrained—Gate A fails.
6. Record both the witness artifacts and the machine-checked theorem. Ground
   checks detect result-bearing oracle failures; they do not replace the
   universal connection theorem.

## Gate A — Real-program soundness

Apply A1–A5 from the shared contract:

1. Confirm program-defined bodies execute or have exact auxiliary execution claims.
2. Compare each bridge's complete state footprint with fixed semantics.
3. Confirm binding, evaluation order, context containment, control, and
   exceptional behavior with the operational-bridge procedure.
4. Apply the result-bearing abstraction procedure, then check equation truth,
   overlap, coverage, descent, and totalization guards.
5. Exhibit a satisfiable witness and run a meaningful false-postcondition mutation.

## Gate A failure: repair before reporting

Every Gate A failure takes this back-edge unless an enumerated, evidenced hard
blocker prevents further repair. Until then, withhold the final status and do
not write `PROOF.md`. First remove or disable every offending extension,
discard `#Top` obtained through it as an unusable proof state, and return to
`proving-spec`. Rerun fixed semantics to expose the genuine residual, repair the
construction, rebuild, recover `#Top`, and restart Gate A within the same agent
invocation.

Only after repair attempts encounter an evidenced hard blocker may validation
select terminal `Incomplete work`. Hard blockers are unavailable required tools
or inputs, an out-of-scope fixed-semantics language gap, repeated external
backend or resource failure, or inconsistent requirements. Record the failed
repair attempts and concrete evidence for the blocker.

A difficult proof is not a hard blocker. A slower safe encoding is not a hard
blocker. Repair that requires redesign is not a hard blocker. `#Top` obtained
only through an unsound shortcut is not a hard blocker and cannot justify
stopping. Keep the original solution and proof artifacts and continue the
one-shot repair loop unless one of the evidenced blockers prevents further
progress.

### A5 non-vacuity procedure

Confirm the proof is discriminating by mutating a result or postcondition to a
small, deliberate false alternative. Choose a mutation that is false for a
satisfiable input, place it in a distinct spec module, and run that artifact.
For the conventional filenames and module names, the exact command is:

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.nix-profile/bin:$PATH"
kprove spec-vacuity.k --definition verification-kompiled \
       --spec-module SPEC-VACUITY || echo "EXPECTED FAILURE"
```

The mutated proof must exit non-zero and produce a stuck claim whose residual
shows the unmet condition. A useful off-by-one residual has this shape:

```
kore-exec: Warning (WarnStuckClaimState):
    The configuration's term unifies with the destination's term, but the
    implication check between the conditions has failed. ...
  { S #Equals S +Int 1 }
[Error] Prover: backend terminated because the configuration cannot be
rewritten further. See output for more details.
```

Record the exact mutation, satisfiable witness, command, exit code, and residual.
If the mutation closes, investigate the precondition, result constraint, and
whether the relevant claims were exercised before reporting success.

## Gate B — Intent adequacy

Restate the formal domain and postcondition in plain language. Compare them with
the source contract, intended property, examples, and material behaviors of the
intended execution model. Distinguish an execution summary from a theorem that
the summary has the requested meaning. Report implementation/specification
disagreements without rewriting the theorem.

Gate B failure with Gate A passing yields `SOUND-BUT-LIMITED`.
This is an honest theorem-status report, not completion of a request for the
full source contract. In particular, finitely many fixed sizes or examples do
not satisfy an unrestricted input domain. Preserve them as partial progress and
do not report the required target proof complete.

## Gate C — Trust and evidence auditability

List every named assumption and its dependents. Verify that every claimed test
artifact exists and record its exact command, input scope, oracle, and result.
Use concrete or differential tests as finite evidence, not universal proof.

### Differential-test procedure

For every summary or trusted abstraction supported by differential testing:

1. Select an independently implemented executable oracle. It must not reuse the
   proof equations or merely restate the abstraction being checked.
2. Compare the proof-side result with the oracle over boundary values, small
   representative values, stated examples, and a documented broader sample of
   the formal domain.
3. Require zero mismatches in the recorded run. One mismatch invalidates the
   claimed empirical support and must remain visible in Gate C.
4. Record the existing test artifact, exact command, complete input scope,
   oracle construction, output, and mismatch count.

These results are evidence about the tested inputs. They do not establish a
universal equivalence, and they do not replace the Gate A obligation to connect
program execution to any abstraction used by the proof.

Gate C failure after Gates A and B pass yields
`FORMALLY-SOUND-UNVALIDATED`.

## Decide and report the status

Record PASS or FAIL for every completed gate. Select a final status only after
Gate A passes or repair attempts encounter an evidenced hard blocker. A hard
blocker leaves `Incomplete work`; after Gate A passes, Gate B failure is
`SOUND-BUT-LIMITED`, Gate C failure is `FORMALLY-SOUND-UNVALIDATED`, and all
three gates passing is `VALIDATED`. Never hide later-gate failures.

## Write PROOF.md

Begin with the exact status. Include, in order: what is proven; formal claim;
proof-extension inventory; exact commands and actual outputs; per-gate results;
trust boundary; empirically supported facts; and excluded behavior.

Preserve the commands actually used. A conventional build and proof record has
this form:

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.nix-profile/bin:$PATH"
kompile --backend haskell verification.k \
        --main-module VERIFICATION \
        --syntax-module SEMANTICS-SYNTAX \
        --output-definition verification-kompiled
kprove spec.k --definition verification-kompiled --spec-module SPEC
# Output: #Top   Exit: 0
```

Do not replace actual outputs with expected outputs. Clearly separate formally
proved facts, conclusions conditional on named assumptions, finite empirical
evidence, and excluded behavior.

## References

- [Running the K tools](../shared/running-k.md) — `#Top` success and stuck-claim
  output needed to interpret proof and mutation runs.
- `proving-spec` — precedes this skill; produces the proof artifacts to audit.
- `writing-spec` — drafts the formal claim; intent adequacy is audited here.

// reference/src/semantics/str.k — MPY-STR

module MPY-STR
  imports MPY-CORE
  imports MPY-ITER

  // ==== iteration (the iterator protocol's str case; yields 1-char strings) ==
  rule <k> #iterNext(str(.IntSeq))                 => #iterDone ... </k>
  rule <k> #iterNext(str(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq)))
        => #iterYield(str(iCons(C, .IntSeq)), str(R)) ... </k>

  // ==== str literal (ASCII-only) ============================================
  syntax IntSeq ::= strToCodes(String) [function]
  rule <k> Str(S:String) => str(strToCodes(S)) ... </k>
  rule strToCodes("") => .IntSeq
  rule strToCodes(S:String) => iCons(ordChar(substrString(S, 0, 1)), strToCodes(substrString(S, 1, lengthString(S))))
    requires S =/=String "" andBool ordChar(substrString(S, 0, 1)) <Int 128

  // ==== operators: + / == / != / in =========================================
  syntax IntSeq ::= seqConcat(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
  rule seqConcat(.IntSeq, T:IntSeq)                => T
  rule seqConcat(iCons(I:Int, S:IntSeq), T:IntSeq) => iCons(I, seqConcat(S, T))

  rule applyBin("+",  str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => str(seqConcat(A, B))
  rule applyCmp("==", str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => A ==K B
  rule applyCmp("!=", str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => notBool (A ==K B)

  // substring membership: `P in X` iff the code-seq P occurs contiguously in X
  rule applyCmp("in",     str(P:IntSeq), str(X:IntSeq)) => strContains(P, X)
  rule applyCmp("not in", str(P:IntSeq), str(X:IntSeq)) => notBool strContains(P, X)

  syntax Bool ::= strPrefix(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
  rule strPrefix(.IntSeq, _:IntSeq)               => true
  rule strPrefix(iCons(_:Int, _:IntSeq), .IntSeq) => false
  rule strPrefix(iCons(A:Int, As:IntSeq), iCons(B:Int, Bs:IntSeq)) => A ==Int B andBool strPrefix(As, Bs)

  syntax Bool ::= strContains(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
  rule strContains(P:IntSeq, X:IntSeq) => true  requires strPrefix(P, X)
  rule strContains(P:IntSeq, .IntSeq)  => false requires notBool strPrefix(P, .IntSeq)
  rule strContains(P:IntSeq, iCons(C:Int, Xs:IntSeq)) => strContains(P, Xs)
       requires notBool strPrefix(P, iCons(C, Xs))

  // ==== lexicographic order: < / <= / > / >= by code point (= Python str order on the code
  // model). strLt reduces on GROUND code-seqs (krun) but is inert/OPAQUE on symbolic ones
  // (a proof's codesProj(V) is an abstract IntSeq — no constructor rule matches), so a symbolic
  // str `<` stays a trusted opaque term the way sortVS / intFloatDiv do. Additive: fires only on
  // str </<=/>/>= comparisons.
  syntax Bool ::= strLt(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
  rule strLt(.IntSeq, .IntSeq)                => false
  rule strLt(.IntSeq, iCons(_:Int, _:IntSeq)) => true
  rule strLt(iCons(_:Int, _:IntSeq), .IntSeq) => false
  rule strLt(iCons(A:Int, As:IntSeq), iCons(B:Int, Bs:IntSeq)) => true          requires A  <Int B
  rule strLt(iCons(A:Int, As:IntSeq), iCons(B:Int, Bs:IntSeq)) => false         requires A  >Int B
  rule strLt(iCons(A:Int, As:IntSeq), iCons(B:Int, Bs:IntSeq)) => strLt(As, Bs) requires A ==Int B

  rule applyCmp("<",  str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => strLt(A, B)
  rule applyCmp(">",  str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => strLt(B, A)
  rule applyCmp("<=", str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => notBool strLt(B, A)
  rule applyCmp(">=", str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => notBool strLt(A, B)
endmodule
// reference/src/semantics/list.k — MPY-LIST

module MPY-LIST
  imports MPY-CORE
  imports MPY-ITER
  imports MPY-OPERATORS

  // ==== iteration (the iterator protocol's list case) =======================
  rule <k> #iterNext(list(.ValSeq))                => #iterDone ... </k>
  rule <k> #iterNext(list(vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq))) => #iterYield(V, list(R)) ... </k>

  // ==== ListExpr: [...] literal -> a fresh heap object =======================
  syntax ApplyK ::= "toList"
  rule <k> ListExpr(ES:Exprs) => #evalArgs(ES, .Vals, toList) ... </k>
  rule <k> #applyK(toList, ACC:Vals) => #alloc(list(vals2valSeq(ACC))) ... </k>

  // ==== list ops: + / == / != ===============================================
  syntax ValSeq ::= valSeqConcat(ValSeq, ValSeq) [function, total]
  rule valSeqConcat(.ValSeq, T:ValSeq)                => T
  rule valSeqConcat(vCons(V:Val, S:ValSeq), T:ValSeq) => vCons(V, valSeqConcat(S, T))

  // list + list constructs a NEW object (k-cell — it allocates; operands land here
  // already deref'd). priority(45) beats the generic BinOp dispatch.
  rule <k> BinOp("+", list(A:ValSeq), list(B:ValSeq)) => #alloc(list(valSeqConcat(A, B))) ... </k>
       [priority(45)]

  rule applyCmp("==", list(A:ValSeq), list(B:ValSeq)) => A ==K B
  rule applyCmp("!=", list(A:ValSeq), list(B:ValSeq)) => notBool (A ==K B)

  // ==== deep equality when elements are heap objects (list-of-lists) ========
  // Python == is structural at every depth. Fires ONLY when a ref is present
  // (the guard decides on concrete seqs); the plain ==K path above is unchanged.
  syntax Bool ::= hasRefVS(ValSeq) [function, total]
  rule hasRefVS(.ValSeq)                => false
  rule hasRefVS(vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq)) => isRefV(V) orBool hasRefVS(R)

  syntax Bool ::= deepEqVS(ValSeq, ValSeq, Map) [function]
                | deepEqV(Val, Val, Map)        [function]
  rule deepEqVS(.ValSeq, .ValSeq, _:Map)                   => true
  rule deepEqVS(.ValSeq, vCons(_:Val, _:ValSeq), _:Map)    => false
  rule deepEqVS(vCons(_:Val, _:ValSeq), .ValSeq, _:Map)    => false
  rule deepEqVS(vCons(A:Val, As:ValSeq), vCons(B:Val, Bs:ValSeq), HP:Map)
    => deepEqV(A, B, HP) andBool deepEqVS(As, Bs, HP)

  rule deepEqV(ref(H:Int), B:Val, HP:Map) => deepEqV({HP[H]}:>Val, B, HP)
       requires H in_keys(HP)
  rule deepEqV(A:Val, ref(H:Int), HP:Map) => deepEqV(A, {HP[H]}:>Val, HP)
       requires notBool isRefV(A) andBool H in_keys(HP)
  rule deepEqV(list(A:ValSeq), list(B:ValSeq), HP:Map) => deepEqVS(A, B, HP)
  rule deepEqV(A:Val, B:Val, _:Map) => A ==K B [owise]

  // ==== mutator: xs.append(v) — an in-place heap write ======================
  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(ref(H:Int), "append")), (V:Val, .Vals)) => noneV ... </k>
       <heap> ... H |-> list(VS:ValSeq => valSeqConcat(VS, vCons(V, .ValSeq))) ... </heap>
       [priority(40)]

  // ==== `x in list` — a <k>-cell fold over #iterNext ========================
  syntax KItem ::= #memberAcc(Val, Iterable) | #memberCont(Val) | "#notB"
  rule <k> Compare(LV:Val, CmpOp("in",     list(VS:ValSeq))) => #memberAcc(LV, list(VS)) ... </k>
  rule <k> Compare(LV:Val, CmpOp("not in", list(VS:ValSeq))) => #memberAcc(LV, list(VS)) ~> #notB ... </k>
// reference/src/semantics/tuple.k — MPY-TUPLE

module MPY-TUPLE
  imports MPY-CORE
  imports MPY-ITER
  imports MPY-LIST
  imports MPY-METHODS

  // ==== iteration (the iterator protocol's tuple case) ======================
  rule <k> #iterNext(tuple(.ValSeq))                => #iterDone ... </k>
  rule <k> #iterNext(tuple(vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq))) => #iterYield(V, tuple(R)) ... </k>

  // ==== TupleExpr: tuple(ValSeq) literal + == != ===========================
  syntax ApplyK ::= "toTuple"
  rule <k> TupleExpr(ES:Exprs) => #evalArgs(ES, .Vals, toTuple) ... </k>
  rule <k> #applyK(toTuple, ACC:Vals) => tuple(vals2valSeq(ACC)) ... </k>

  rule applyCmp("==", tuple(A:ValSeq), tuple(B:ValSeq)) => A ==K B
  // membership routes through the same k-cell fold as lists (list.k)
  rule <k> Compare(LV:Val, CmpOp("in",     tuple(VS:ValSeq))) => #memberAcc(LV, tuple(VS)) ... </k>
  rule <k> Compare(LV:Val, CmpOp("not in", tuple(VS:ValSeq))) => #memberAcc(LV, tuple(VS)) ~> #notB ... </k>
  // t.index(v): first index of v (ValueError out of subset)
  rule applyMethod(tuple(VS:ValSeq), "index", V:Val, .Vals) => idxOfVS(VS, V, 0)
  syntax Int ::= idxOfVS(ValSeq, Val, Int) [function]
  rule idxOfVS(vCons(A:Val, _:ValSeq), V:Val, I:Int) => I requires A ==K V
  rule idxOfVS(vCons(A:Val, R:ValSeq), V:Val, I:Int) => idxOfVS(R, V, I +Int 1)
       requires notBool (A ==K V)
  rule applyCmp("!=", tuple(A:ValSeq), tuple(B:ValSeq)) => notBool (A ==K B)

  // ==== target binding: bind a Name or a TupleExpr target to a value ========
  syntax KItem ::= #bindTgt(Expr, Val)
  rule <k> #bindTgt(Name(X:String), V:Val) => .K ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ X <- V ], _) ... </scopes>
  rule <k> #bindTgt(Name(X:String), V:Val) => #cellW({M[X]}:>Val, V) ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
       requires "$cells" in_keys(M)
        andBool pnMember(X, cellsOf({M["$cells"]}:>Val))
        andBool X in_keys(M) andBool isCellRef({M[X]}:>Val)
       [priority(40)]
  rule <k> #bindTgt(TupleExpr(TS:Exprs), tuple(VS:ValSeq)) => #unpackSeq(TS, VS) ... </k>
  rule <k> #bindTgt(TupleExpr(TS:Exprs), list(VS:ValSeq))  => #unpackSeq(TS, VS) ... </k>
  rule <k> #bindTgt(TupleExpr(TS:Exprs), ref(H:Int)) => #bindTgt(TupleExpr(TS), V) ... </k>
       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
       [priority(40)]

  // ==== unpacking: a, b = <tuple|list> (RHS evaluated by strictness) ========
  syntax KItem ::= #unpackSeq(Exprs, ValSeq)
  rule <k> Assign(TupleExpr(TS:Exprs), tuple(VS:ValSeq)) => #unpackSeq(TS, VS) ... </k>
// reference/src/semantics/float.k — MPY-FLOAT
//
// Minimal, TRUSTED float support. K/Haskell (kprove) has no usable symbolic IEEE-754 theory and
// no Int2Float hook, so a float value stays an OPAQUE proof-domain primitive: `intFloatDiv(I, F)`
// (the Python true division I / F) is `[no-evaluators]` for kprove — it never reduces on symbolic
// input, and the proof verifies only the STRUCTURE (the result is the exact term the program
// builds). The `[concrete]` rule evaluates it for krun (llvm HAS the Int2Float / /Float hooks), so
// smoke tests run the real float value.
//
// Only the pieces needed so far: Float as a Val, the float literal, and Int / float true division
// (the `a * h / 2.0` idiom). More float ops (float +/-/*, comparison) are added as float problems
// need them — kept minimal + sound.

module MPY-FLOAT
  imports MPY-OPERATORS
  imports MPY-BUILTINS
  imports FLOAT

  // Float is a value; the float literal evaluates to the K Float.
  syntax Val ::= Float
  rule <k> Float(F:Float) => F ... </k>

  // Int / float true division. OPAQUE for kprove (no-evaluators); concrete for krun.
  syntax Float ::= intFloatDiv(Int, Float) [function, total, symbol(intFloatDiv), no-evaluators]
  rule intFloatDiv(I:Int, F:Float) => Int2Float(I, 53, 11) /Float F [concrete]

  rule applyBin("/", I:Int, F:Float) => intFloatDiv(I, F)

  // Int / Int true division (Python: always a float). OPAQUE for kprove; concrete for krun.
  syntax Float ::= divII(Int, Int) [function, total, symbol(divII), no-evaluators]
  rule divII(I1:Int, I2:Int) => Int2Float(I1, 53, 11) /Float Int2Float(I2, 53, 11) [concrete]
  rule applyBin("/", I1:Int, I2:Int) => divII(I1, I2)

  // float % float (e.g. `number % 1.0` = the fractional part). OPAQUE for kprove, concrete for
  // krun. Python's float `%` is floor-based: a % b = a - floor(a/b)*b (K's %Float is IEEE
  // remainder, which differs — 3.5 %Float 1.0 = -0.5 vs Python 0.5 — so it is NOT used).
  syntax Float ::= floatMod(Float, Float) [function, total, symbol(floatMod), no-evaluators]
  rule floatMod(F1:Float, F2:Float) => F1 -Float (floorFloat(F1 /Float F2) *Float F2) [concrete]
  rule applyBin("%", F1:Float, F2:Float) => floatMod(F1, F2)

  // float equality — for concrete krun asserts (e.g. `area == 7.5`); the FLOAT.eq hook is fine on
  // concrete floats. kprove proofs return floats structurally and do not compare them.
  rule applyCmp("==", F1:Float, F2:Float) => F1 ==Float F2
  rule applyCmp("!=", F1:Float, F2:Float) => notBool (F1 ==Float F2)

  // float `<` and abs — OPAQUE for kprove ([no-evaluators], so a SYMBOLIC float compare stays an
  // uninterpreted Bool a proof case-splits on — a SINGLE compare per branch, not a nonlinear cascade),
  // [concrete] for krun. Additive, sort-disjoint from the Int rules. (has_close_elements: the pairwise
  // `abs(a-b) < t` proximity test.)
  syntax Bool ::= floatLt(Float, Float) [function, total, symbol(floatLt), no-evaluators]
  rule floatLt(F1:Float, F2:Float) => F1 <Float F2 [concrete]
  rule applyCmp("<", F1:Float, F2:Float) => floatLt(F1, F2)

  syntax Float ::= absF(Float) [function, total, symbol(absF), no-evaluators]
  rule absF(F:Float) => absFloat(F) [concrete]
  rule applyBuiltin("abs", F:Float, .Vals) => absF(F)

  // ==== math.ceil ===========================================================
  // `import X` is a no-op (we intercept the specific math functions syntactically; `math` itself is
  // never bound as a value).
  rule <k> Import(_:String) => .K ... </k>

  // math.ceil(x): ceiling to an int. Intercepted at the Call BEFORE `math` is looked up (higher
  // priority than the generic Attribute/method dispatch in call.k).
  syntax KItem ::= "#mathCeil"
  rule <k> Call(Attribute(Name("math"), "ceil"), (E:Expr, .Exprs)) => E ~> #mathCeil ... </k> [priority(40)]
  rule <k> V:Val ~> #mathCeil => ceilF(V) ... </k>

  // math.floor(x) — same interception shape as math.ceil
  syntax KItem ::= "#mathFloor"
  rule <k> Call(Attribute(Name("math"), "floor"), (E:Expr, .Exprs)) => E ~> #mathFloor ... </k> [priority(40)]

// Bool operator cases + the truthy boolean operations (not / and / or; and-or are

module MPY-BOOL
  imports MPY-CORE

  rule applyUn("not", V:Val) => notBool truthy(V)

  rule applyCmp("==", B1:Bool, B2:Bool) => B1 ==Bool B2
  rule applyCmp("!=", B1:Bool, B2:Bool) => B1 =/=Bool B2

  // ==== BoolOp: short-circuit, value-returning and / or =====================
  // the node is its own accumulator: heat the HEAD element only, then either return it
  // (short-circuit) or drop it and continue
  context BoolOp(_, (HOLE:Expr, _:Exprs))
  rule <k> BoolOp(_:String, (V:Val, .Exprs)) => V ... </k>
  rule <k> BoolOp("and", (V:Val, A:Expr, REST:Exprs)) => BoolOp("and", (A, REST)) ... </k>
       requires truthy(V)
  rule <k> BoolOp("and", (V:Val, _:Expr, _:Exprs)) => V ... </k>
       requires notBool truthy(V)
  rule <k> BoolOp("or",  (V:Val, _:Expr, _:Exprs)) => V ... </k>
       requires truthy(V)
  rule <k> BoolOp("or",  (V:Val, A:Expr, REST:Exprs)) => BoolOp("or", (A, REST)) ... </k>
       requires notBool truthy(V)

  // ==== heap-object head: decide truthiness THROUGH the heap, never rewrite the
  // operand — and/or return the OBJECT itself (Python identity), not its structure
  rule <k> BoolOp(_:String, (ref(H:Int), .Exprs)) => ref(H) ... </k>
       [priority(40)]
  rule <k> BoolOp("and", (ref(H:Int), A:Expr, REST:Exprs)) => BoolOp("and", (A, REST)) ... </k>
       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
       requires truthy(V)
       [priority(40)]
  rule <k> BoolOp("and", (ref(H:Int), _:Expr, _:Exprs)) => ref(H) ... </k>
       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
       requires notBool truthy(V)
       [priority(40)]
  rule <k> BoolOp("or", (ref(H:Int), _:Expr, _:Exprs)) => ref(H) ... </k>
       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>

// The operator DISPATCH layer: operands evaluate by strictness (heat/cool over KResult=Val),
// the cooled node hands to applyUn/applyBin/applyCmp (declared in core.k; each domain file
// owns its cases — bool.k, int.k, float.k, str.k, list.k, tuple.k, set.k, dict.k).

module MPY-OPERATORS
  imports MPY-CORE
  imports MPY-ITER

  rule <k> UnaryOp(OP:String, V:Val) => applyUn(OP, V) ... </k>

  rule <k> BinOp(OP:String, L:Val, R:Val) => applyBin(OP, L, R) ... </k>

  // Compare's right operand sits under the CmpOp wrapper — contexts instead of attributes
  context Compare(HOLE, _)
  context Compare(_:Val, CmpOp(_, HOLE))
  rule <k> Compare(LV:Val, CmpOp(OP:String, RV:Val)) => applyCmp(OP, LV, RV) ... </k> [owise]

  rule applyCmp("is",     V:Val, noneV) => V ==K noneV
  rule applyCmp("is not", V:Val, noneV) => notBool (V ==K noneV)

  // ==== operand deref: heap objects combine/compare by STRUCTURE ============
  // (Python: list == is structural; identity only via `is`.) priority(40)
  // preempts the generic dispatch so applyUn/applyBin/applyCmp never see a ref.
  rule <k> BinOp(OP:String, ref(H:Int), R:Expr) => BinOp(OP, V, R) ... </k>
       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
       [priority(40)]
  rule <k> BinOp(OP:String, L:Val, ref(H:Int)) => BinOp(OP, L, V) ... </k>
       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
       requires notBool isRefV(L)
       [priority(40)]

  // the left operand of `in`/`not in` is an ELEMENT (compares by ==K) — never deref'd
  rule <k> Compare(ref(H:Int), CmpOp(OP:String, R:Expr)) => Compare(V, CmpOp(OP, R)) ... </k>
       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
       requires OP =/=String "in" andBool OP =/=String "not in"
       [priority(40)]
  rule <k> Compare(L:Val, CmpOp(OP:String, ref(H:Int))) => Compare(L, CmpOp(OP, V)) ... </k>
       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
       requires notBool isRefV(L)
        orBool OP ==String "in" orBool OP ==String "not in"
       [priority(40)]

  rule <k> UnaryOp(OP:String, ref(H:Int)) => UnaryOp(OP, V) ... </k>
       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
       [priority(40)]
endmodule

  // ==== math.ceil ===========================================================
  // `import X` is a no-op (we intercept the specific math functions syntactically; `math` itself is
  // never bound as a value).
  rule <k> Import(_:String) => .K ... </k>

  // math.ceil(x): ceiling to an int. Intercepted at the Call BEFORE `math` is looked up (higher
  // priority than the generic Attribute/method dispatch in call.k).
  syntax KItem ::= "#mathCeil"
  rule <k> Call(Attribute(Name("math"), "ceil"), (E:Expr, .Exprs)) => E ~> #mathCeil ... </k> [priority(40)]
  rule <k> V:Val ~> #mathCeil => ceilF(V) ... </k>

  // math.floor(x) — same interception shape as math.ceil
  syntax KItem ::= "#mathFloor"
  rule <k> Call(Attribute(Name("math"), "floor"), (E:Expr, .Exprs)) => E ~> #mathFloor ... </k> [priority(40)]
  rule <k> V:Val ~> #mathFloor => floorFI(V) ... </k>
  syntax Int ::= floorFI(Val) [function, total, symbol(floorFI)]
  rule floorFI(I:Int)   => I                        [concrete]
  rule floorFI(F:Float) => Float2Int(floorFloat(F)) [concrete]

  // bare floor/ceil (bound by `from math import floor, ceil`)
  rule applyBuiltin("floor", V:Val, .Vals) => floorFI(V)
  rule applyBuiltin("ceil",  V:Val, .Vals) => ceilF(V)

  // math.pow(x, y) — a two-arg interception onto powF (ints promote)
  syntax KItem ::= #mathPow1(Expr) | #mathPow2(Val)
  rule <k> Call(Attribute(Name("math"), "pow"), (E1:Expr, E2:Expr, .Exprs)) => E1 ~> #mathPow1(E2) ... </k> [priority(40)]
  rule <k> V1:Val ~> #mathPow1(E2:Expr) => E2 ~> #mathPow2(V1) ... </k>
  rule <k> V2:Val ~> #mathPow2(V1:Val) => powF(toF(V1), toF(V2)) ... </k>
  syntax Float ::= toF(Val) [function, total, symbol(toF)]
  rule toF(F:Float) => F        [concrete]
  rule toF(I:Int)   => intToF(I) [concrete]

  // ceilF: math.ceil as an Int. TOTAL (K trusts it; a symbolic list element stays opaque for
  // kprove — structural). [concrete] so the Int2Float/ceilFloat hooks only run for krun (llvm).
  // Matches Python incl. negatives: ceil(-2.4) = -2 = Float2Int(ceilFloat(-2.4)).
  syntax Int ::= ceilF(Val) [function, total, symbol(ceilF)]
  rule ceilF(I:Int)   => I                       [concrete]
  rule ceilF(F:Float) => Float2Int(ceilFloat(F)) [concrete]

  // unary minus on a float (e.g. the literal -2.4 = UnaryOp("-", Float(2.4))). Concrete for krun;
  // proofs use symbolic elements, never a float literal.
  rule applyUn("-", F:Float) => 0.0 -Float F

  // ---- float - / / / + (OPAQUE for kprove [no-evaluators], concrete for krun) — for float-list
  // element maps (x - lo) / (hi - lo). Mirror intFloatDiv: additive, sort-disjoint from the Int rules.
  syntax Float ::= subF(Float, Float) [function, total, symbol(subF), no-evaluators]
  rule subF(F1:Float, F2:Float) => F1 -Float F2 [concrete]
  rule applyBin("-", F1:Float, F2:Float) => subF(F1, F2)

  syntax Float ::= divF(Float, Float) [function, total, symbol(divF), no-evaluators]
  rule divF(F1:Float, F2:Float) => F1 /Float F2 [concrete]
  rule applyBin("/", F1:Float, F2:Float) => divF(F1, F2)

  syntax Float ::= addF(Float, Float) [function, total, symbol(addF), no-evaluators]
  rule addF(F1:Float, F2:Float) => F1 +Float F2 [concrete]
  rule applyBin("+", F1:Float, F2:Float) => addF(F1, F2)

  syntax Float ::= mulF(Float, Float) [function, total, symbol(mulF), no-evaluators]
  rule mulF(F1:Float, F2:Float) => F1 *Float F2 [concrete]
  rule applyBin("*", F1:Float, F2:Float) => mulF(F1, F2)

  syntax Float ::= powF(Float, Float) [function, total, symbol(powF), no-evaluators]
  rule powF(F1:Float, F2:Float) => F1 ^Float F2 [concrete]
  rule applyBin("**", F1:Float, F2:Float) => powF(F1, F2)

  // ---- the remaining comparisons (gtF promoted from find_zero — its summaries
  //      case-split on the atom; >= / <= derive from the two opaque compares) ----
  syntax Bool ::= gtF(Float, Float) [function, total, symbol(gtF), no-evaluators]
  rule gtF(F1:Float, F2:Float) => F1 >Float F2 [concrete]
  rule applyCmp(">",  F1:Float, F2:Float) => gtF(F1, F2)
  rule applyCmp(">=", F1:Float, F2:Float) => notBool floatLt(F1, F2)
  rule applyCmp("<=", F1:Float, F2:Float) => notBool gtF(F1, F2)

  // ---- mixed Int/Float operators promote the Int side (n ** 0.5 etc.) ----
  rule applyBin("**", I:Int, F:Float) => powF(intToF(I), F)
  rule applyBin("**", F:Float, I:Int) => powF(F, intToF(I))
  rule applyBin("-",  I:Int, F:Float) => subF(intToF(I), F)
  rule applyBin("-",  F:Float, I:Int) => subF(F, intToF(I))
  rule applyBin("+",  I:Int, F:Float) => addF(intToF(I), F)
  rule applyBin("+",  F:Float, I:Int) => addF(F, intToF(I))
  rule applyBin("*",  I:Int, F:Float) => mulF(intToF(I), F)
  rule applyBin("*",  F:Float, I:Int) => mulF(F, intToF(I))

  // ---- mixed Int == Float (shared eqF; opaque symbolic / concrete twin) ----
  syntax Bool ::= eqF(Float, Float) [function, total, symbol(eqF), no-evaluators]
  rule eqF(F1:Float, F2:Float) => F1 ==Float F2 [concrete]
  rule applyCmp("==", I:Int, F:Float) => eqF(intToF(I), F)
  rule applyCmp("==", F:Float, I:Int) => eqF(F, intToF(I))
  rule applyCmp("!=", I:Int, F:Float) => notBool eqF(intToF(I), F)
  rule applyCmp("!=", F:Float, I:Int) => notBool eqF(F, intToF(I))
  rule applyCmp("<",  I:Int, F:Float) => floatLt(intToF(I), F)
  rule applyCmp("<",  F:Float, I:Int) => floatLt(F, intToF(I))
  rule applyCmp(">",  I:Int, F:Float) => gtF(intToF(I), F)
  rule applyCmp(">",  F:Float, I:Int) => gtF(F, intToF(I))

  // ---- x == None (promoted from 137; `is` cases live in operators.k) ----
  rule applyCmp("==", V:Val, noneV) => V ==K noneV
  rule applyCmp("!=", V:Val, noneV) => notBool (V ==K noneV)

  // ---- float(str): decimal parse (promoted from 137's defined chain) ----
  // digits '.' digits, optional leading '-'; concrete evaluation only (the
  // symbolic side stays an opaque decStrToF term a proof case-splits on).
  syntax Float ::= decStrToF(IntSeq) [function, total, symbol(decStrToF), no-evaluators]
+ sed -n 1,26p /reference/k-proof/reference-semantics/semantics/operators.k
// reference/src/semantics/operators.k — MPY-OPERATORS
// The operator DISPATCH layer: operands evaluate by strictness (heat/cool over KResult=Val),
// the cooled node hands to applyUn/applyBin/applyCmp (declared in core.k; each domain file
// owns its cases — bool.k, int.k, float.k, str.k, list.k, tuple.k, set.k, dict.k).

module MPY-OPERATORS
  imports MPY-CORE
  imports MPY-ITER

  rule <k> UnaryOp(OP:String, V:Val) => applyUn(OP, V) ... </k>

  rule <k> BinOp(OP:String, L:Val, R:Val) => applyBin(OP, L, R) ... </k>

  // Compare's right operand sits under the CmpOp wrapper — contexts instead of attributes
  context Compare(HOLE, _)
  context Compare(_:Val, CmpOp(_, HOLE))
  rule <k> Compare(LV:Val, CmpOp(OP:String, RV:Val)) => applyCmp(OP, LV, RV) ... </k> [owise]

  rule applyCmp("is",     V:Val, noneV) => V ==K noneV
  rule applyCmp("is not", V:Val, noneV) => notBool (V ==K noneV)

  // ==== operand deref: heap objects combine/compare by STRUCTURE ============
  // (Python: list == is structural; identity only via `is`.) priority(40)
  // preempts the generic dispatch so applyUn/applyBin/applyCmp never see a ref.
  rule <k> BinOp(OP:String, ref(H:Int), R:Expr) => BinOp(OP, V, R) ... </k>
       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
